doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

chapter: Condon's circle and New York scene
title: A brief office job
summary: He quit a thirty-dollar-a-week office job because weddings paid more.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Did you have to work non-music jobs on the way up?

I did one gig. I did one job that lasted about six months. I had fallen in love with a girl when I was about nineteen years old, some gal in Brooklyn, and she didn’t like the idea that I was playing my weddings and doing that on weekends. And she’d be by herself. And so I decided that maybe I should get a career, you know. Dumb kid in love at nineteen. So I got a job in an office and did that for a while and found out that I was making more on the weekends playing those two wedding jobs or whatever it was, than it was with the whole week. I mean jeez, I was making like thirty dollars a week, taking a subway back and forth every day. It was ridiculous. I mean those are bad wages in those days, but I guess they were average. But it was minimum wage, that thirty bucks. But I’d wind up making thirty-five, forty on the weekends. And I said hey, what am I doing knocking myself out. And I decided that I wasn’t in love. No this isn’t love.
I guess she didn’t become your wife?
No. No that’s an old story. That’s another story. We’ll do that on another interview.
Oh my. Well see 19 — you said this is the early 50s?
